_comment: notifybridge example config. Deploy with config/deploy-config.ps1 (pushes to /data/local/tmp/notifybridge.json). No config file at all = bridge fully passive. Every event source is its own section (notifications/broadcasts/settings) with a flat out list; the optional global 'routes' table matches across all sources. Route grammar: 'action' = posted/removed/on/off ('*' any), 'category' = the routing split (exact value / '*' any / '' only none - for notifications the normalized category 'call' / 'missed_call' / the app's own / '' when none), 'pkg' filters by package (exact or 'prefix*', default '*'). Broadcast/settings routes are self-contained: their trigger fields (action/event/polarity/snapshot/fields and table/name/event/defaultOn) pick the event, to/line route it; one trigger may fan out over several routes to different sinks. Every matching route fires (routing is a fan-out): to route one event to different lines per package, list specific-pkg routes and do NOT mix a '*' route for the same action on the same sink - the package hits both and the sink gets two lines. The old 'when' key and the per-entry 'out' nesting are gone (dropped with a warning). Unknown/extra keys are ignored; an unknown 'action' inside notifications.out is dropped with a warning.

notifications._comment: NotificationListenerService source. enabled:false (or omitting the whole section) stops notification listening entirely. Every notification is one notify event; call classification runs on ANY package by notification markers (category CALL, a 'call'-ish channel, answer/decline/end-call actions) and picks the route category - a live call is 'call' ($incoming rides along, $reason on removal), a missed-call tombstone (channel contains 'missed') is 'missed_call', everything else keeps the app's own category or '' if it set none. The bridge does NOT decide SIM vs messenger - the config does, one line per package: telephony dialers render as RING_*, messenger/voip apps as VOIP_*; a live call from any other package only ever matches the raw ENQ/CAN routes below. To forward a call from a new app, add a posted/removed pair with its package. To forward only a few apps, set 'pkg' on the raw routes instead of '*'. To keep a live call off the raw pool entirely, drop the ENQ/CAN pair or narrow their 'category'.

broadcasts._comment: System broadcasts: one section, flat out list. Each route is self-contained - its trigger (action/event/eventAction/polarity/snapshot/fields) picks the event, to/line route it. One intent action may fan out over any number of routes to different sinks (repeat the action+event). A route without 'action', 'event' or 'to' is dropped with a warning. Registering the receiver delivers sticky states (BATTERY_CHANGED) by itself. The old nesting (entry with its own out) is gone.

settings._comment: Watch Settings keys and forward changes through inline routes. One flat out list; route fields: table (system|global|secure), name (watched key), event (bus event type, the route category), defaultOn (polarity when the key is missing/unreadable), to, line. One name may fan out over several routes.

routes._comment: Global routes match across every source - this is the raw-tube / cross-source hook. 'action':'*' + 'category':'*' mirrors everything; an action-only route catches every polarity event of that action.
